claims.text: The initial as-cast magnetic high-entropy alloy is single-phase and has a relatively homogeneous microstructure with moderate coercivity.
Aging at approximately 500°C for 2 hours followed by controlled cooling will induce nanoscale, coherent secondary-phase precipitates.
The aging treatment will produce uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates coherently embedded in the primary matrix.
The nanoprecipitates may be Cr-rich or compositionally similar secondary phases.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Pinning by the nanoprecipitates increases the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
The increased barrier to domain-wall motion produces a higher coercive field than in the untreated alloy.
The aged alloy will have a higher coercive field than the matched as-cast baseline.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase will correlate with nanoprecipitate density and distribution.
The coercivity-enhancing effect requires precipitates to remain below 50 nm and to have an appropriate volume fraction.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency could negate the domain-wall-pinning effect.
Large deviations from the target aging temperature or duration may cause precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency.
The optimal aging temperature and duration may vary with alloy composition.
